methods.label: Chain rule
methods.explanation: \((x^2)'\) evaluated at \(2x\) is \(2\times(2x)\), then multiply by \(2\). At \(x=1\), the result is \(8\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the square derivative and the simple affine chain rule.

methods.label: Simplify the composition first
methods.explanation: Substitute \(2x\) into the given formula for \(f\) before differentiating. Then \(y=f(2x)=(2x)^2=4x^2\), so the power and constant-multiple rules give \(y'=8x\). Hence \(y'(1)=8\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the square of a product and basic polynomial differentiation instead of the chain rule.
